chunks: By Allah, no sudden death came upon me that I disliked,
and I was but like a traveler who reached (his destination), and a seeker who found (his aim),
And whatever is with Allah is the best for the righteous ones.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe his death in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this poignant passage from his final will, Imam Ali (AS) demonstrates the consummate *Rida* (contentment) of the Ahl al-Bayt by reframing death not as a loss, but as the inevitable arrival of a long-awaited guest. This metaphor of the traveler reaching a spring underscores the Shia theological view of death as a transition to divine proximity, a concept deeply rooted in the verse from Surah Al-Imran (3:198) which he cites to affirm that ultimate bliss resides with Allah. The narration serves as a practical model for believers to face mortality with the serenity of one who has completed their worldly duty and is now entering the eternal realm.

en.sayed-ali-raza: By Allāh, this sudden death is not an event that I dislike,
nor is it an accident that I hate.
I am just like a night traveller who reaches the spring (in the morning) or like or seeker who secures (his aim):
And whatever is with Allāh is the best for the righteous ones. (Qur’ān, 3:198)
